question: can I do some paid freelance work outside my job here?
answer: Yes, a few hours a month of paid side work is fine if done in personal time and it doesn't affect your PostHog work.
evidence: p965: A few hours a month on a paid side gig is acceptable.

followUp.question: do I need to run it by anyone first?
followUp.standalone: Do I need anyone's approval before doing paid freelance work outside PostHog?
followUp.answer: Yes, check in with the relevant Exec team member for your team (James, Tim, or Charles) and get their confirmation first.
followUp.evidence: p966: check in with the relevant Exec team member for your team (ie. James, Tim, or Charles)

question: who started posthog and when?
answer: James (Hawkins) and Tim (Glaser) founded PostHog on January 23, 2020.
evidence: p1028: PostHog was founded by James and Tim on January 23, 2020.

question: a big prospect wants a feature promised by Q3 written into their contract - is that ok?
answer: No. PostHog doesn't contract deliverables, especially not by a date; it only builds for a big customer if others will use it too.
evidence: p808: We don't contract deliverables, and we especially don't contract to provide deliverables by a certain date.

question: how does a YC founder get a desk at Hogpatch?
answer: Only by invitation: it's invite-only, founders can't apply, PostHog handpicks from a waitlist when space opens, and invites last 3 months.
evidence: p944: We do maintain a waitlist, but you can't apply - we handpick founders when there's room to welcome more.

question: why did US customers lose their older Logs data in February?
answer: A ClickHouse bug in experimental zero-copy replication deleted the S3-stored data parts for every replica of the Logs cluster.
evidence: p137: A bug in ClickHouse caused it to unexpectedly attempt to delete almost all of the data parts in S3.

followUp.question: did we get any of it back?
followUp.standalone: Was any of the US Logs data lost in the February 2026 incident recovered?
followUp.answer: Only the most recent ~3 days, backfilled from Kafka's 3-day retention; data older than that was lost.
followUp.evidence: p139: Configuring Kafka with 3 days of retention saved us from total data loss for recent activity.

question: we're launching a beta soon - when do we need to start tracking which users are interested in our product?
answer: As soon as the product is in any kind of public beta, start capturing product intents, before any public release.
evidence: p462: As soon as your product is in any sort of public beta you should start tracking product intents.

question: which of my accounts are big enough to be worth visiting in person?
answer: Accounts paying or likely to pay $50k+/year with expansion, renewal or major hurdles; the expansion guide says regularly see $100k+ accounts.
evidence: p561: In-person visits work best for accounts paying or likely to pay $50k+/year

question: a customer is organizing a dev meetup and asked us for money - how much do we usually chip in?
answer: Typically between $500 and $3,500, and the support usually comes with some added PostHog engagement.
evidence: p822: Budgetary support typically falls in the range from $500 to $3,500.

question: how do I pull the posthog org IDs for all my accounts out of salesforce?
answer: Run a SQL query on salesforce.account selecting distinct posthog_org_id_c where owner_id is your Salesforce ID, then export to CSV.
evidence: p240: SELECT DISTINCT posthog_org_id_c, NULL as empty_column FROM salesforce.account WHERE owner_id = 'your_salesforce_id'

question: how can I see what posthog is doing on a customer's live site?
answer: Add ?__posthog_debug=true to a page URL on their site to turn on debug mode, which shows PostHog logs and config.
evidence: p1060: Debug mode: append ?__posthog_debug=true to a site that has posthog running

followUp.question: what about checking if they've set up a reverse proxy?
followUp.standalone: How can I check whether a customer is using a reverse proxy?
followUp.answer: Look at api_host in their PostHog config; us.i.posthog.com or eu.i.posthog.com means no reverse proxy, their own domain means one.
followUp.evidence: p1060: To check if a customer is using a reverse proxy, look at their api_host configuration.
